correctness.rationale: Commutation with a disjoint-union-of-chains nilpotent partial injection forces each source chain domain either empty or an initial segment of length s and image a terminal segment of a target chain of the same s, where 1<=s<=min(source length,target length); injectivity makes participating source-target chains a partial permutation. The weight of each edge is t^s, giving Cλ weighted rook polynomial. Iterating along a chain-label directed cycle only creates an actual periodic vertex if all positional offsets λ_target−s vanish; cyclic inequalities force all participating lengths equal and decorations full length. Sign inclusion-exclusion over these fully aligned equal-size cycles evaluates sum_{π∈S_m}(-1)^cycles(π)=0 for m>=2, leaving at most one selected chain of each distinct length; exactly Nλ(t)=Σ_{T⊆H}(-1)^|T|∏(m_h t^h)C_{λ\T}(t). For equal L, labeled paths/cycles with weights w_L and subtracting all-full cycles give N-EGF=(1−t^L z)C-EGF, hence the rank-shift coefficient identity. Independently enumerated every partial injective map in seven chain partitions totaling up to 5 vertices, checked commutation and actual nilpotence, and matched exact coefficient lists to the signed sieve. Includes L=1 singleton and empty cases.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge qualified PASS only for the rank-refined nilpotent centralizer cycle-cancellation identity and its simple uniform-chain rank shift, not for characterizing commuting maps. Konieczny (2013) Theorem 3.4 already supplies the structural chain normal form; Gomes–Howie (1987) characterize nilpotent partial injections generally; Laradji–Umar (2004) count unrestricted nilpotent elements. These results do not state the signed deletion sieve of nilpotents in a specified nilpotent centralizer. Konieczny 2020 focuses Green relations and second centralizers in the accessible abstract; its full primary text remains inaccessible via authorized institutional VPN and could contain implicit equivalents.

value.rationale: The intersection of nilpotent elements with the centralizer of a fixed nilpotent partial bijection, stratified by rank, is a natural finite inverse-semigroup enumeration problem. Cycle cancellation converts a large signed sum over cycles to an exact 2^|H| sum indexed by distinct chain lengths for all chain partitions, and uniform chains have an especially sharp rank-shift identity. It provides structural coefficients not supplied by a bare commuting-element classification or unconditioned nilpotent count.
